newsitem.title: HUNGARY: WEIGHTLIFTING-BELARUSSIAN DOPE TESTS NOT FINAL - IWF. [corrected 15:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: WEIGHTLIFTING-BELARUSSIAN DOPE TESTS NOT FINAL - IWF. [corrected 15:40 GMT]

text.p: Preliminary urine tests on five Belorussian weightlifters have detected traces of banned anabolic substances, the International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) said on Tuesday.
"This is the result of the A (first) test and our policy is not to make any official announcement until the B tests are concluded," Agnes Lukacsfalvi of the IWF told Reuters.
She added that results of the conclusive B tests would be known in the second half of June.
Belarus Weightlifting Federation sources named the five as Andrei Marchenko, Vladimir Khlud, Alexei Krushevich, Ruslan Doroshevich and Fyodor Mager.
Lukacsfalvi said she did not know whether the preliminary findings would endanger the Belarus squad's participation in this week's European championships in Croatia.
She added, however, that according to IWF rules any national federation with more than three positive drugs tests within a year faces a one-year ban or possible fines.
(corrects from ..."a one year ban and possible fines.") Belarus is, with Russia, one of the world's great weightlifting powers.
Alexander Kurlovich, a double Olympic medallist in 1992 who took over as Belarus chief coach only a few months ago, himself suffered two doping suspensions in major world competitions.
Marchenko represents Belarus in the 76 kg class, Khlud in 91 kg, Mager at 108 kg and Krushevich and Doroshevich both lift in the over 108 kg category.
